A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same survey, with matching sections, equations, figures, and dataset catalogue. All nine pages of v1 and eleven pages of v2 are readable. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reviews results attributed to prior work. Table 1 catalogues datasets, and Figure 2 illustrates potential confounders; neither reports original experimental or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v2 remains a literature survey without original empirical results. Its added SpuCo entry describes a resource attributed to Joshi et al. (2023), without evaluating it.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same method families and descriptions of existing algorithms. Neither version introduces an original model or learning procedure.

E1.justification: SpuCo is added to Section 4.1 and Table 1 as a surveyed dataset, not as data actually used for training or evaluation by this work. Neither version conducts its own benchmark evaluation.

E2.justification: The methods reviewed in Section 3 remain the same. Neither PDF reports an evaluated comparator set, and the added SpuCo citation does not introduce a baseline comparison.

E3.justification: Neither version specifies an experimental protocol executed by this work. Section 4.2 retains the same worst-group, average-group, and bias-conflicting accuracy metrics.

E4.justification: No ablations, robustness experiments, sensitivity analyses, or case-study findings are added or removed. Figure 2 retains the same illustrative MIMIC-CXR images and highlighted potential confounders.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty estimates for original results.

E6.justification: The qualitative findings attributed to reviewed methods remain unchanged, and neither version supplies experimental performance tables. SpuCo's added statistics and the combined VQA sample count are dataset-catalogue metadata, not new empirical outcomes.

T1.justification: Definition 1 becomes Definition 2.1 without changing its mathematical content. Equations (1)–(5) and their assumptions remain unchanged; no proofs or theoretical results are added.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the claimed first survey, formal definition, method taxonomy, dataset and metric overview, and future research directions. Removing 'comprehensive' from the abstract does not change the contribution scope retained in the introduction and conclusion.

C2.justification: Section 5 preserves the discussion of group-label requirements, worst-group versus average-performance tradeoffs, benchmark limitations, and foundation-model opportunities and risks. No substantive interpretation or applicability qualification changes.

D1.justification: No implementation instructions, hyperparameters, hardware details, or code/data access procedures are added or revised. The SpuCo addition provides catalogue metadata and a citation.

R1.justification: v2 adds Joshi et al. (2023), 'Towards mitigating spurious correlations in the wild: A benchmark & a more realistic dataset,' and includes SpuCo in Section 4.1 and Table 1. This modestly extends literature coverage without revising the survey's positioning.

P1.justification: Small edits replace 'biased' with 'non-essential' in the abstract and introduction and trim evaluative wording elsewhere. Xia Hu and the Rice University affiliation are removed. Section order and almost all explanatory prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 retains the two-column format and both figures while changing headers, citation and caption styling, and figure placement and sizing. Table 1 adds SpuCo and combines IV-VQA and CV-VQA into one row: 657,090 plus 59,513 becomes 716,603.

improvement.justification: Adding SpuCo and its citation modestly improves the survey's usefulness as a dataset reference. Combining the VQA rows loses their separate sample counts while preserving the total, a small reduction in detail. The methodological synthesis and scientific claims remain intact, so the overall improvement is limited.
